For this project, I'm interested in how reported childcare capacity varies across Baltimore ZIP codes. I'll explore the MDPS Early Childhood data to compare program records, program settings, and capacity for different age groups. I'll also check missing information and repeated addresses before interpreting the comparisons.

I want to see how childcare programs and their reported capacity vary across Baltimore ZIP codes. I’m also interested in whether different program settings have different schedules and serve different age groups.

I’m starting by looking through the table, checking what needs cleaning, and trying a few charts. I’m using the course’s EDA notes to help organize the process. At this point, I’m looking for patterns and figuring out which comparisons are actually useful.

1. Inspect the columns and clean the data.
2. Check missing information and possible duplicate records.
3. Summarize childcare capacity by ZIP code.
4. Compare program counts, capacities, and program settings.
5. Write short notes about the patterns in the results.

Starting by using https://umbc-viz.github.io/ges778/notes/05_eda.html to structure this EDA. First, I’m loading the packages and making a working copy of the data. I’m removing rows without an address so I can focus on the program records.

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hide', fig.show='hold', warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#| label: setup

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(cowplot)

```
These are the libraries used if not already installed use install.packages().

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hold'}
#| label: import-data

childcare_eda <- read.csv(
  "../data/MDPS Early Childhood Dev.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(address),
    address != ""
  )
```
The original table had seven footnote rows at the bottom. Filtering out rows without addresses lets me keep those notes in the original file without including them in the analysis.

The count of program records in each ZIP code will be crucial. These counts are the number of programs offered in the zip not there capacity.

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hold', fig.show='hold'}
#| label: Histogram_Function

capacity_histogram <- function(variable, bins = 40){ 
  ggplot(childcare_eda, aes(x = {{ variable }}))+
    geom_histogram(
      bins = bins, fill = "navy", color = "white"
    ) + 
    labs(
      x = "Reorted Capacity", y = "Number of Program Records"
    )
}

capacity_histogram(total_capacity_1) + 
  labs(title = "FUNCTION EXAMPLE: Total Childcare Capacity")
```
Since I want several similar histograms, I'm making a function so I can change the column without rewriting the chart. The bins control how the values are grouped into bars.

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hold', fig.show='hold', warning=FALSE}
#| label: infant-capacity-histogram

childcare_eda$Infant.Capacity.. <- as.numeric(
  as.character(childcare_eda$Infant.Capacity..)) 
capacity_histogram(Infant.Capacity.., bins = 25) +
  labs(title = "Infant capacity")

capacity_histogram(Center.Toddler.Capacity, bins = 25) +
  labs(title = "Toddler capacity")

capacity_histogram(Preschool.Capacity, bins = 25) +
  labs(title = "Preschool capacity")

capacity_histogram(School.Age..capacity..., bins = 25) +
  labs(title = "School-age capacity")
```
The Infant.Capacity code was not working properly since it wasn't numeric this was because the data set had footnotes in the bottom 7 rows as next.Line 105 is us shifting the characters to numeric. I'm using these to check the spread of capacities and see whether a few large programs stand out from the smaller ones. Missing values are left out of the histograms.

```{r, echo=TRUE}
#| label: Density_Zip-capacity

# https://umbc-viz.github.io/ges778/extras/summarizing.html

programs_zip <- childcare_eda |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    zipcode %in% c(zipcode),
    !is.na(total_capacity_1),
    total_capacity_1 <= 300
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    zipcode = as.character(zipcode)
  )

zip_avg <- programs_zip |>
  dplyr::group_by(zipcode) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    capacity_mean = mean(total_capacity_1)
  )

zip_avg
```

I'm keeping capacities of 300 or less this is to cover every program capacity. I used zipcodes as the category since it was the best field to aggregate too. I would've preferred to use neighborhoods and if i was to develop further this would be the way. 

If doing spatial analysis this can be developed further. 

The product of this gives the average program capacity for each zipcode. These averages can develope a solid comparison of program acessibility over space. 

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hold', fig.show='hold'}
#| label: Density_Zip-capacity_chart

ggplot(
  programs_zip,
  aes(x = total_capacity_1, fill = zipcode)
) + 
  geom_density(alpha = 0.2)+
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = capacity_mean, color = zipcode),
    data = zip_avg,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of program capacity by ZIP code",
    subtitle = "Vertical lines show mean program capacity",
    x = "Reported capacity per program",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "ZIP code",
    color = "ZIP code"
  )
```
This is not usable but has a good example of the data i wish to continue examining. The curves show how program sizes are distributed within each zipcodes, and the vertical lines show the averages.

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hold'}
#| label: Capcity_Days-Open

program_day <- childcare_eda |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(total_capacity_1),
    total_capacity_1 <= 300
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      
      Monday.Open,
      Tuesday.Open,
      Wednesday.Open,
      Thursday.Open,
      Friday.Open,
      Saturday.Open,
      Sunday.Open
    ),
    names_to = "day",
    values_to = "open"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(open == "Yes") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    day = factor(
      day,
      levels = c(
        "Monday.Open",
        "Tuesday.Open",
        "Wednesday.Open",
        "Thursday.Open",
        "Friday.Open",
        "Saturday.Open",
        "Sunday.Open"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "Mon",
        "Tue",
        "Wed",
        "Thu",
        "Fri",
        "Sat",
        "Sun"
      )
    )
  )

program_day_avg <- program_day |>
  dplyr::group_by(day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    capacity_mean = mean(total_capacity_1)
  )

program_day_avg
```
I made these columns in the excel before bringing into here. The time_days_open column was laid out with each day ex. ["Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday","Saturday","Sunday"] this seemed unnecessarily difficult to adjust so the other columns were made. 

Before i started the analysis here in R i spent time making columns in the table placing the days in the DAY.Open columns. I marked the days they were open as yes/no based off if they gave a times for when open/closed on that day. 

While not a chart this is showing a curve that drops during the skews sligly in the middle of the week then drops off during the weekend. 

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hold', fig.show='hold'}
#| label: Capcity_Days-Open_Chart

ggplot(
  program_day,
  aes(x = total_capacity_1, fill = day)
) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(
    aes(xintercept = capacity_mean, color = day),
    data = program_day_avg,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Program capacity by day open",
    subtitle = "Programs with capacity of 200 or less, lines show the means",
    x = "Reported capacity per program",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Day open",
    color = "Day open"
  )
```
This chart compares the sizes of childcare programs open on each day. The x-axis shows reported capacity, the colors represent different days, and the vertical lines show each day’s average program capacity. Its use case seems limited as the data is so clustered the visualization isnt great. 

Density shows where program sizes are concentrated. Using the capacity we can find the averages for each day.

The curves here are the percentage of programs capacity on the different days. The massive spike shows that on saturday has 47% of its programs with a capacity of 5-10 spaces. 

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hold'}
#| label: heatmap_program-avaibility-setup

day_order <- c(
  "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday",
  "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"
)

availability <- childcare_eda |>
  select(
    setting = gen_program_setting_detail,
    ends_with(".Time")
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = ends_with(".Time"),
    names_to = c("day", ".value", NA),
    names_sep = "\\."
  ) |>
  mutate(
    opening = as.numeric(as.difftime(trimws(Start), units = "hours")),
    closing = as.numeric(as.difftime(trimws(End), units = "hours")),
    day = factor(day, levels = day_order)
  ) |>
  tidyr::drop_na(opening, closing) |>
  tidyr::uncount(24, .id = "hour") |>
  mutate(
    hour = hour - 1,
    open = ifelse(
      closing < opening,
      hour >= opening | hour < closing,
      hour >= opening & hour < closing
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(setting, day, hour) |>
  summarise(
    percent_open = mean(open) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::complete(setting, day, hour = 0:23)
```
Here I’m getting the schedules ready for the heatmap. I put each program-day on its own row and turn the opening and closing times into numbers, so 6:30 becomes 6.5. Then I drop days without usable times instead of counting them as closed.

Next, I make one row for each hour from 0 to 23 and check whether the program is open at the start of that hour, including schedules that go past midnight. I group these checks by setting, day, and hour, then average them to get the percentage open. This follows the grouped-average approach from the course notes. Finally, I add missing combinations back so every setting has a full week displayed, while keeping those values missing.

```{r, echo=TRUE, results='hold'}
#| label: heatmap_program-avaibility
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 10

ggplot(
  availability,
  aes(x = hour, y = day, fill = percent_open)
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ setting, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 23, 2),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    limits = rev(day_order),
    labels = function(x) substr(x, 1, 3),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "grey95",
    high = "navy",
    limits = c(0, 100),
    na.value = "grey95"
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_colorbar(
      direction = "horizontal",
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekly Childcare Availability",
    subtitle = "By MDPS program setting",
    x = "Time of day",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "% Of Open Programs",
    caption = paste0(
      "Only program-days with usable opening and closing times are included.\n",
      "Grey represents both unschedule information and times.\n",
      "Source: MDPS Early Childhood dataset (2026)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 12),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold", size = 20, color = "navy"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(b = 35)),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(1, 1.06),
    legend.justification = c(1, 0),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: availability-weekdays-weekends
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6

availability |>
  mutate(
    day_group = ifelse(
      day %in% c("Saturday", "Sunday"),
      "Weekends",
      "Weekdays"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(setting, day_group, hour) |>
  summarise(
    percent_open = mean(percent_open, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = percent_open, color = setting)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ day_group) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 23, 4),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 25)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
  values = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "#808000"))(
    dplyr::n_distinct(availability$setting)
  )
) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekday and Weekend Childcare Availability",
    subtitle = "By MDPS program setting",
    x = "Time Of Day",
    y = "% of Open Programs",
    color = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Daily percentages are averaged equally within weekdays and weekends; missing days are excluded.\n",
      "Only program-days with usable opening and closing times are included.\n",
      "Source: MDPS Early Childhood dataset (2026)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 12),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, color = "navy"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

```{r}
#| label: program-setting-share-setup

program_setting_chart <- childcare_eda |>
  filter(!is.na(zipcode)) |>
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = factor(zipcode),
      fill = gen_program_setting_detail
    )
  ) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill")
```

```{r}
#| label: program-setting-share-chart
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7

program_setting_chart +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
  values = colorRampPalette(c("navy", "grey95"))(
    dplyr::n_distinct(childcare_eda$gen_program_setting_detail)
  )
) +
  labs(
    x = "ZIP code",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    title = "Childcare Program Settings by ZIP Code",
    subtitle = "Share of program records in each setting",
    caption = "Source: MDPS Early Childhood dataset (2026)."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "black"),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, color = "navy"),
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      margin = margin(t = 8)
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.justification = c(1, 0.95),
    legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.5, "lines"),
    legend.key.height = grid::unit(1, "lines"),
    legend.key.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.1, "lines")
  )
```
Looking through this, I’m becoming more interested in the relationship between program setting and opertaing schedules. Regestered family childcare homes make up the largest group of records, followed by licensed childcare centers. Among programs with capacity of 300 or less, those reporting weekend operation have a lower average capacity than those reporting weekday operation, around 15 spaces compared with 28. I want to explore whether differences in program settings help explain that pattern. These results describe reported programs and schedules, though, rather than available openings or whether childcare meets local demand. I steped back and took time to develop the last three charts to have a full picture; Program by zipcodes shows the disterbution of programs in each zip. The other two are displaying the same thing in different ways, i like the heatmap more but think the variation is truly seen in the faceted line chart.
